hypothesis: Decoding each int4 group once and reusing it across prompt rows is faster than unpacking the same nibbles on every row, and the per-row FMA order stays bit-identical.
model: synthetic fmt=4 gs=64, S=32 I=2048 O=1024, not a checkpoint
command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ./tests/bench_i4g_blk (8 kernel calls per sample; tok_s is calls/second)

hardware.cpu: Intel Xeon (KVM), 4 vCPU, AVX2+AVX-512; kernel is the AVX2 path
hardware.storage: not on the timed path (weights are in RAM)

config.kernel: decode group once, reuse across rows
